transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I'm mainly here because I'm having some trouble at work. I'm a nurse, and... I just lose my train of thought constantly on the floor. 

Like, if an IV pump beeps, or... a call light goes off, or even if someone just asks another nurse a question... I just suddenly forget what patient flow issue I was working on. So... yeah. That's mainly why I'm here.
When did you first notice these problems with losing your train of thought? Has this always been something you've struggled with, or is this more recent?

Um... I guess it's been a major issue for a while now. Maybe... almost two years? 

That's when I took on the expanded charge-nurse responsibilities, so... yeah. Since then, mostly.

Before you took on the charge-nurse role two years ago, when you were doing regular nursing duties, did you have similar problems with focus and attention, or is this really something new that started with the expanded responsibilities?

Um... no, it's not exactly new. I guess it's always been there, just... maybe not as obvious. 

Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was... bright, but careless. I was always losing worksheets or just... forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to sit with me every single night just to keep me on track with it. So... yeah, it's been around for a while.
Besides work and school, have you noticed similar problems with attention and focus in other areas of your life—like at home, in social situations, or with hobbies or personal projects?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. Just with... routine things, mostly. 

Like paying a bill at home, or... forgetting to call a family member back. Sometimes I just don't show up for an appointment. Even when I fully meant to go, or... even if I actually set a reminder for it. It just slips my mind. 

Same with... following up on a missing order, or whatever. Just... things like that, I guess.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety? Like, do you have trouble sitting still, or do you feel like you need to be moving around or doing something with your hands?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I do that. I mean, I sit still just fine.
When you're working or doing tasks that require focus, do you find yourself tapping your feet, bouncing your leg, or moving around more than other people seem to?
No, I don't really do that either. I mean... I might shift in my chair sometimes, but not more than anyone else, I don't think. I'm usually pretty still.
Do you find yourself acting without thinking things through first? Like, do you interrupt people, blurt things out, or make quick decisions that you later regret?

Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think I do that. I usually keep to myself in conversations, so... interrupting isn't really an issue. And I'm pretty cautious about decisions, I think. So... no.

You mentioned these attention problems at work, school, and home. Overall, how much have they been affecting your ability to function and your quality of life? Would you say they're causing you significant trouble, or are they more of a minor annoyance?

Um... it's... it's pretty bad. I mean, it's causing a lot of trouble. At work, it's gotten to the point where... well, I'm on formal supervision now. And the other nurses... they have to double-check some of my charge-nurse follow-through. It's... embarrassing. I just feel like I'm becoming a liability instead of a leader. So, yeah. It's not just a minor annoyance.
When you're sitting at work or at home, do you ever feel like you have excess energy or feel like you need to do something physical, even if you're not actually moving around a lot?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't feel like that. I just feel tired mostly. Not... energetic.
Have you ever done things on impulse that got you into trouble—like spending money you didn't have, or taking risks without thinking about the consequences?
No, I don't think so. I'm... I'm pretty careful with things like that.
Looking back to your elementary school years, do you remember how old you were when your teachers first started noticing these problems with attention and forgetfulness?

Um... I guess it was pretty early on. Even in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was... bright, but careless. I was always losing my worksheets or... forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to sit with me every night just to... keep me on track. So, yeah, it's been a long time.
When you think back to your childhood, do you remember having these attention and forgetfulness problems before you turned 12 years old?

Um, yeah... like I just said, it was back in elementary school. So, definitely before I was 12. That's when... you know, the teachers were saying I was careless and losing my worksheets. And my mom was having to sit with me every night to do my homework. So... yes.
Have you ever been evaluated or diagnosed with ADHD—attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder—by a doctor before, or have you ever been on any medications for attention or focus problems?
Um, no. I haven't. I've never been tested for it... or taken any medication like that.

You mentioned these attention problems at work, at school back then, and at home with bills and appointments. Are there any areas of your life where you don't struggle with focus and attention—like hobbies you enjoy, activities you're interested in, or things you're passionate about?
Um... I don't know. I guess... not really. I mean, even with things I like, I still... drift off. So, no, not really.
